note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Bacchus (1997), a monographic revision, Microtermes in East Africa; the original treats the alate, soldier and major worker, and only the alate section is taken here; figure numbers, type specimens and synonymic discussion are omitted; the measurement table is misaligned in the OCR and no numbers from it are cited.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep yellow; frons and genae paler; vertex with many pale yellow punctures of various sizes scattered at the hair bases; fontanelle a small pale brown dot; anteclypeus yellowish white; postclypeus, antennae, labrum and pronotum yellow; abdominal tergites pale yellow, the sternites paler; legs pale yellow, tibiae and tarsi sometimes slightly darker than the femora. Wings pale yellow, the costa darker. Posterior margin of the head capsule arcuate, evenly rounded; setae numerous above the compound eyes and few behind them, none extending beyond the eye bulge; vertex slightly concave or not concave around the fontanelle; a low median ridge extending forwards from near the fontanelle; epicranial suture incomplete, weak or absent; frons smooth, sloping gently towards the postclypeus; postclypeus shield-shaped, the median line absent or distinct. Compound eyes and ocelli oval; labrum shorter than wide; antennae 15/16-segmented, segment 3 shortest, segments 1, 2 and 4 subequal. Pronotum with numerous setae.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with the head capsule deep yellow, the postclypeus shield-shaped with the median line either absent or distinct, and the antennae 15/16-segmented with segment 3 the shortest; it differs from other species of the genus mainly in the evenly arcuate posterior margin of the head capsule, the sparse setae behind the compound eyes and the density of the pronotal pilosity.
